text:
olivia: Heads up — inference p99 spiking across a subset of us-east hosts since ~08:10. correlates with packet drops on host NICs :eyes:

matt: are these the dedicated GPU nodes or shared hosts?

olivia: dedicated-gpu pools (pool-g4-us-east-2). I pulled a quick iftop and saw lots of retransmits between hosts.

jana: can you run `tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` on one of the affected boxes? thinking qdisc might've been changed during the morning infra push.

olivia: running now, paste follows:
```
$ tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc tbf 1: root refcnt 2 rate 1000Kbit burst 1600b lat 50ms
 Sent 12345678 bytes 34567 pkt (dropped 4321, overlimits 213)
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
qdisc fq_codel 10: parent 1:2 limit 1000 flow_limit 1024 quantum 1514 ecn __active__
 Sent 23456789 bytes 45678 pkt (dropped 0, overlimits 0)
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 10
```

suresh: that tbf is the smoking gun — someone applied a 1Mbps host throttle as part of the morning QoS change. tbf with tiny burst = per-host egress bottleneck, kills east-west RPCs for KV cache and increases inference tail.

matt: who rolled that? infra-bot, any rollout id for a tc playbook today?

infra-bot: rollout 2026-03-18/qa-qos-policy v2 applied to pool-g4-us-east-2 at 08:05 by automation (ansible). change id: rl-4521

oncall-ryan: Ack. rolling back on canary nodes now. Quick mitigation: remove tbf and restore fq_codel root.

oncall-ryan: commands I'm running on canary:```
sudo tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root fq_codel limit 1000
# or to delete the tbf entirely
sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root
```

jana: after rollback on 3 canaries p99 dropped back to normal within ~2m, retransmits stopped. good sign.

olivia: capturing tc stats to confirm across fleet. also seeing small MTU mismatch logs on some hosts — might be unrelated but noting: `ip link show` shows mtu 9000 on some, 1500 on others which could make bursts worse across tunnels.

suresh: yeah keep an eye on MTU. but primary failure mode was the accidental tbf throttle. playbook had a missing inventory filter so it targeted gpu hosts.

matt: action items:
- rollback rl-4521 fleet-wide for now (infra)
- update playbook to exclude dedicated-gpu pools / add canary gating (infra)
- run a quick sweep `tc -s qdisc show` and collect dropped counters (sre)
- follow up on MTU inconsistencies (networking)

olivia: opened a ticket and linked the infra PR: https://git.redwood.internal/infra/ansible/rl-4521 — added logs + tc output.

infra-bot: rollback job queued: rl-4521-revert -> starting canary rollback on 5 hosts.

oncall-ryan: will monitor inference SLOs and keep this thread updated. thanks all :thumbsup:

matt: postmortem once we stabilize. prefer to add an automated qdisc safety check to the host-provisioner (reject tbf below X rate on dedicated pools).

olivia: agreed. patching the provisioning guard now.

suresh: FYI — if anyone needs to repro locally, you can simulate with `tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 1mbit burst 1600 latency 50ms` then run a simple RPC load to see p99 blow up quickly.

jana: marking this thread resolved once rollback completes and SLOs stable for 30m.
